experiment: R101 ColBERT late-interaction retrieval, fold-0, A100 (CORRECTED after user pushback)
note: First run was UNDER-POWERED (query truncated to 32 tokens; 1 epoch). User correctly flagged it. Fixed: query_length=128, more epochs, +20k train-split (matching BGE regime).
verdict: colbertv2.0 (BERT-base late-interaction), fairly tested + full-data, PLATEAUS at recall@300 0.43 -- ~63% of fine-tuned BGE-large (0.68), recall@20 0.18 << prod 0.48, 7 unique recoveries. Loses clearly. The limiter is base-encoder strength (BERT-base 110M vs BGE-large 335M), NOT the late-interaction mechanism or doc length (earlier 'docs too short' hypothesis was WRONG).
caveat_blocked: GTE-ModernColBERT (strong ModernBERT base + late interaction) is the truly fair test but is BLOCKED in this env: needs sentence-transformers>=4 (kernel has 3.0.1) + kernel restart + full re-run. torch.compile import bug already fixed via no-op monkeypatch; only the ST-version wall remains.
pattern: Every retriever tested now underperforms fine-tuned BGE-large: E5-large, GTE-Qwen2-7B (zero-shot), cross-encoder rerank (R100), ColBERT-v2 (R101). BGE-large remains best. nDCG ceiling for our methods holds at production R92 p11 (0.5073).
